extracted.intended_audience: life-science researchers, journal editors, and science communicators interested in post-publication peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for conducting, moderating, and responding to post-publication peer review (PPPR) in the life sciences, including platform choice, anonymity trade-offs, speed, and effects on the scientific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous post-publication assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous post-publication assessment of papers is crucial for the filtering and potential integration of meritorious data into the scientific collective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPPR should aim to evaluate the quality and merits of published work so that valid findings can be integrated into the scientific record; rigorous assessment can be faster than traditional review and helps reduce waste in science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: PPPR is faster than traditional forms of evaluation and can catalyze concrete outcomes—corrections and retractions—much more rapidly than older mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid identification of problems (examples: STAP cell case, MBD3 debate) shows that timely PPPR can prevent wasted resources and protect trainees; timeliness is a key value when assessing PPPR effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform selection and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of web platforms (F1000, ResearchGate, PubPeer, blogs, PubMed Commons, bioRxiv, Twitter) strongly influences uptake, audience, anonymity, and impact of PPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different platforms have different cultures (e.g., F1000 focused on positive reviews; PubPeer often anonymous); consider platform moderation, reach (MozRank example), and norms when deciding where to post or look for PPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance constructive critique with avoiding a 'gotcha' mentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Much PPPR is negative and sometimes intensely so; a minority express concern over a 'gotcha' mentality in which criticism is non-constructive and targeted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should also note strengths of papers and aim for constructive, balanced commentary; scientific community should brainstorm ways to counteract a predominantly negative culture to maximize PPPR's positive impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity protects reviewers from retaliation but can embolden non-constructive criticism, targeted attacks, sockpuppetry, and can impede productive dialogue because identities are unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh safety benefits of anonymity against costs (e.g., litigation, false identities); consider policies that enable accountability while protecting legitimate whistleblowers; anonymity management is central to PPPR quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation, comment filtering, and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Better moderation, comment filtering, a set of standards, and even a proposed PPPR editorial board have been suggested to manage potential downsides of PPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing moderation and clear standards can reduce non-constructive comments and legal exposure; platforms and community governance should consider these mechanisms to improve PPPR civility and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of unpublished data in commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters might be reluctant to publicly back-up challenges with unpublished data for fear of being scooped or inadvertently creating 'prior publication'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concern limits data-based give-and-take during PPPR; communities/journals should clarify whether posting such data constitutes prior publication and consider mechanisms to allow secure data sharing to support critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with journal-based post-publication mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal-based responses (letters, rebuttals) sometimes are slow or may be rejected, and journals may be reluctant to publish critiques that could lead to retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPPR often avoids journal-centered delays, but effective post-publication correction of the record requires interplay between PPPR and journals; evaluate whether journals transparently handle and respond to post-publication critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to reproducibility, accuracy, and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: PPPR has the potential to improve the quality of research, make science more efficient and accurate, and reduce waste by accelerating correction of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess PPPR efforts by their ability to detect errors, prompt corrections/retractions, and improve reproducibility; emphasize mechanisms that translate PPPR findings into formal corrections when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding targeted or personal attacks and legal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: PPPR comments have sometimes been targeted at individuals and have led to litigation (example of lawsuit over anonymous PubPeer comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters and platforms should avoid personal attacks; platforms need policies to manage defamatory or targeted content and to mitigate legal risks for both commenters and hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to enable productive scientific dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing with whom one is engaged facilitates fruitful give-and-take discussions; anonymity can be a roadblock to constructive exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When safe and appropriate, encourage transparency of commenter identity or verified credentials to promote constructive, evidence-backed discussions and enable follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community cultural acceptance and generational shift
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of PPPR has grown due to a cultural shift toward internet norms and broader acceptance within the life sciences community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that uptake depends on cultural factors; efforts to normalize constructive PPPR (training, exemplars, platform norms) can accelerate positive adoption across generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of social media and real-time platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: PPPR sometimes occurs in real time on social media (e.g., Twitter), which facilitates rapid dissemination but may have limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social media for rapid highlights and links to deeper critiques, but rely on moderated platforms or full posts for substantive, evidence-backed critiques to avoid miscommunication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging platforms with moderation/endorsement (e.g., NIH/PubMed Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderated venues such as PubMed Commons, and institutional involvement, can encourage and legitimize PPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support or develop moderated platforms that provide clear policies and editorial oversight to improve the quality and trustworthiness of PPPR contributions.
